speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are a newborn with increasing yellow discoloration of your eyes and skin; this suggests jaundice. To understand the severity and cause, have you noticed any dark urine, pale stools, or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (Physiologic).

The clinical picture of a 2-week-old exclusively breastfed infant with increasing jaundice, normal weight gain, and no signs of cholestasis (dark urine/pale stools) or infection (fever) is classic for insufficient intake jaundice due to breastfeeding. No further tests are required at this time.
